newsitem.title: USA: Stocks moderately higher after opening surge.
newsitem.headline: Stocks moderately higher after opening surge.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks were moderately higher in heavy trading Friday after a powerful opening rally attributed to the "triple-witching" futures and options expirations steadily lost steam.
At 1 p.m., the Dow Jones index was up 36.14 points at 6,509.78 after surging more than 70 points in the opening minutes of the session.

Analysts said the fierce opening rally was due to the so-called triple-witching expiration of futures and options Friday, a factor that also contributed to extremely heavy NYSE volume of more than 420 million shares.
Advances led declines 15 to 9 on the NYSE.

Volume was very high and analysts said the session could see a new record on the NYSE because another burst of activity was likely in the closing minutes. The current volume record, set July 16, is 680.3 million shares.
Analysts said there were clear signs the market was headed higher at the opening bell.

As frequently occurs on triple-witching sessions -- when institutions square huge positions linked to stock options, index options and futures contracts -- trading on many issues could not begin because of order imbalances that were pushing opening prices higher.

"The buy-side imbalances were huge at the open," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. What was significant, though, was that, "Nasdaq turned around almost immediately."
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 7.71 points to 1,288.15.

The Nasdaq decline was linked to a broad sell-off in technology stocks, which were almost completely left out of the initial rally. Instead, more defensive stocks like banks and pharmaceuticals dominated the buying interest.

"We saw people getting themselves positioned in classic defensive plays," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "You're seeing some money come off the table in some other industries."
The rotational move suggested to many analysts that the Dow might not have much momentum left after a powerful three-day charge of more than 200 points.
"People are looking at a more defensive situation," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "I would guess we're going to stay rangebound as we head into the new year."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 4/32, raising its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.60 percent from 6.59 percent at Thursday's close.
Among technology stocks, International Business Machines Corp. fell 3-3/8 to 154-3/4 and Intel Corp. dipped 2-1/8 to 135-3/8.
Among banks, J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. rose 1-1/2 to 99-1/2, BankAmerica Corp. rose 1 to 101-5/8 and NationsBank Corp. climbed 1-3/8 to 99-5/8.
In individual issues, Dendrite International Inc. plummeted 11-1/2 to 8-1/8, one day after announcing it would lose money in its fourth quarter.
Redhook Ale Brewery Inc. tumbled 4-1/2 to 9-1/2. The company said Thursday its fourth-quarter results would be below expectations.
